intro.title: @supports
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that uses the @supports rule to apply different styles based on browser support for specific CSS features. You will learn how to use @supports to check if a browser supports a CSS property or value, and then conditionally apply styles accordingly. The main technology involved is the CSS @supports at-rule, which allows you to write feature queries. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to creating more robust and forward-compatible CSS by gracefully handling browser differences.
intro.usecase: The @supports rule is essential for creating progressive enhancement strategies in modern web applications. Developers use it to conditionally apply CSS features like CSS Grid or Flexbox layouts in dashboards and data tables, ensuring they work across different browser versions. For example, a responsive admin panel might use @supports to implement advanced grid layouts in modern browsers while falling back to simpler float-based layouts in older ones. This pattern is also valuable for implementing cutting-edge UI features like CSS custom properties in design systems or backdrop-filter effects in modal dialogs, providing graceful degradation without breaking the user experience.
